content.comment_body: I have three [product_name] ([article_no]). The first one was programmed two years ago and has been working reliably since. Now, I'm trying to set up the other two, but despite attempts throughout the year, they fail to operate over the network. Locally, the program works and tests successfully. The issue arises when I attempt to communicate with the module; it does not connect as expected. I've configured the module on my network with IP 10.10.10.103 and my computer uses IP 10.10.10.10. Running [product_name] [version_no], I tried upgrading, but [company_name] reports no available upgrade. I added the device with IP 10.10.10.103, accessed the Online Settings, and the test button confirms with a green tick. However, when attempting to assign an IP address, I get the error: "The connected Base Module does not support network communication." The module is detected during the interface search, but further actions fail. What could be wrong in my approach? Any advice is welcome.

Hello [user_name], welcome to the forum. Was your PC's IP address two years ago also 10.10.10.10? What subnet mask do your PC and the [product_name] use? Did you purchase the other two devices recently? They might have different [article_no]s, for example, [article_no] instead of [article_no], and you would require at least [product_name] [version_no]. Please confirm this. Also, upgrading to the latest version of [product_name] is free. You can download it from [url]. The upgrade is a full package about 1.3 GB in size. After downloading, install it as Administrator.

Thanks for the helpful forum. I purchased all three devices together and the first one works fine. My computer's IP address now is the same as before and I'm using the same machine. The subnet is 255.255.255.0. When checked, the device configuration is: IP 10.10.10.101, subnet 255.255.255.0, gateway 10.10.10.1. My computer uses the same subnet.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is able to program and test [product_name] devices locally, but encounters a network communication error when attempting to assign an IP address using [product_name] software. The message suggests the base module does not support network communication, causing uncertainty since older hardware has worked successfully. There is confusion regarding hardware and software compatibility and a misunderstanding about the availability of software upgrades.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipates straightforward network configuration and IP setup for all [product_name] modules using [product_name] software, without facing issues related to compatibility or configuration.
